successors.note: 'In 1885, the Transvaal government only allocated a small territory to the Pedi, with the majority of the people living outside of it.' The British held Transvaal 1877-1881 (Transvaal annexed in April 1877).

capitals.name: Manganeng on the Steelpoort River (stand-in inside Sekhukhuneland)
capitals.note: APPROXIMATE: the Sekwati page says that under Thulare 'the capital was Manganeng, situated on the Steelpoort River' (around the turn of the 19th century) and gives no coordinates; the gazetteer has no place in Sekhukhuneland (its only places in 24-25.6S, 29.2-30.6E are Lebowakgomo, Polokwane and Tzaneen, all outside), so the dot is the centre of the hint box for Sekhukhuneland (29.5-30.5E, 24.2-25.2S), south of the Steelpoort. [Repair 2026-10-19: the earlier stand-in was Polokwane (29.45E, 23.89S), north of the 24.0S edge of the K0 box and of Sekhukhuneland.]

capitals.name: Phiring, then Thaba Mosego (stand-in inside Sekhukhuneland)
capitals.note: APPROXIMATE, same stand-in point: Sekwati 'strategically chose Phiring, a mountain stronghold, as his base' after his exile (no year) and, after the 1852 siege, 'moved his capital from Phiring to Thaba Mosego' (Mosega Kop, chiefly for its water); the page gives no year for either move or for Sekhukhune's seat.  The Sekhukhune page adds that he 'lived on a mountain, now known as Thaba Leolo or Leolo Mountains', which he fortified (no years), and that after the battle of 2 August 1876 Burgers retreated 'to Steelpoort, where a fort was built' (Krugerpos).

ledger.note: c. 1826: Thulare's outer lands are lost in the Mfecane. Sekwati page: 'Around 1826, the Ndebele under Mzilikazi seized the opportunity and overthrew the Pedi regime', killing several of Thulare's sons; Swazi campaigns against the Pedi 'failed to take their mountain strongholds' (undated). The Pedi people page names 'Ndwandwe invaders from the south-east' without a year; the Sekwati page does not mention the Ndwandwe. The region is the researcher's reading (the box beyond Sekhukhuneland). [Repair 2026-10-19: was 1820, confidence 1, counterpart ndwandwe-kingdom, which has no matching gain and dissolves in 1820 with its land to zululand; now 1826, confidence 2, counterpart nobody, the same land that ndebele-kingdom /ledger/1 takes from nobody in 1826 around Rustenburg and Pretoria. The Pedi page's Ndwandwe and this page's Ndebele are not reconciled.]

certainty.note: No frontier is described; the Pedi polity was a paramountcy of the Maroteng over tributary chiefdoms.

notes: Cliopatria has no Pedi. One page opened (Pedi people; the article Pedi_Empire did not load: URL_NOT_FOUND). The page gives no capital and no area; the capital point is a stand-in; the Thulare box is the page's three place names (Rustenburg, lowveld, Vaal) turned into a polygon. The end date is 1882 (monarchy dismantled); the page offers 1879 (defeat), 1882 and 1885 (a small reserve) as markers. The Zwide/Ndwandwe invasion has no date on the page. Counterparts needing dossiers: ndwandwe-kingdom (c. 1790-1820), swazi-kingdom (written below), and union-of-south-africa for the later land. Gazetteer name needed: region Sekhukhuneland (Limpopo/Mpumalanga, south of the Steelpoort River).
